findings.comedy_and_timing: Occupancy declaration is a short pause after noisy motion; slipper success has a visible stillness beat. Max paw-check literalizes his confusion, and following the relocated foot earns Both feet, then? Buddy losing several wonderful seconds links his peaceful choice to the interruption. The gnome remaining cheerful gives the opposing threat no actual menace.
findings.voices_and_agency: Neet stays disproportionately combative; Max stays gentle and puzzled; Heather punctures Neet with practical removal and affectionate size comparison. Buddy seeks rest, moves the slipper, selects flowers, leaves them, tries his own bark and finally retrieves Neet. His final decision changes the outcome rather than merely commenting.
findings.causality_and_emotion: Wake-up leads to kitchen refuge; park conflict causes Heather to carry Neet; arriving home exposes the gnome; invitation alone fails, while Buddy nose contact brings Neet inside. Shared slipper transforms Buddy initial exclusion into chosen companionship. Final two short paragraphs give the callback room without an explanatory coda.
findings.breakfast_placement: After Neet accepts Occupied and resumes patrol; Buddy eyes closed and Neet walking away, not still sniffing slipper. Heather matching slipper and sock add quiet context without new plot.
findings.max_placement: After Max raises one paw, before Buddy leaves flowers and before rear-leg bouncing. Current V005 visibly preserves all three states. Large gentle figure against small barking dog supplies scale comedy, and distant Buddy sniffing supplies competing desire.
findings.gnome_placement: After tentative supporting bark and before Buddy sits. Both dogs stand and unequal mouth openings distinguish commitment. Smiling stationary gnome carries the comic nonresponse.
